title: Culture and position

blocks.heading: Culture and position
blocks.text: Cultural values and practices influence expectations about work, property and participation. They can support cooperation or restrict opportunities depending on their form and use; culture is diverse and changing, not a fixed explanation of all women’s experiences.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Values
blocks.text: Values concern what people regard as desirable or acceptable. A value placed on mutual support may encourage shared work, while an expectation that leadership belongs to one gender can restrict voice. Explain the mechanism rather than stereotyping a community.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Customs
blocks.text: Customs and practices shape how social decisions are carried out. A meeting timetable or speaking arrangement can affect who participates. Consultation can reveal whether a practice supports or restricts access and what affected people want changed.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Taboos and myths
blocks.text: A taboo restricts an activity or discussion; a myth may be used to explain or justify a belief. If a belief excludes women from a productive role regardless of skill, it narrows opportunity. Describing that effect does not endorse the belief or claim it is shared by all members.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Read the practical connection
blocks.text: In a fictional savings group, important decisions are made while some members are collecting children from school. Written membership rights do not give those members an effective voice at that time. Consultation over meeting times and a way to submit views can improve participation. Such arrangements should respond to the actual members’ duties rather than assume that all women share the same responsibilities.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated
